data.reply: Queue #723 (note 1020), from your two-player Frontier night of 24 Oct. Measured on frontier:7 with 2, 3 and 4 bots, 6 nights each. Today a crew of two meets as many monsters a night as a crew of three (19.5 against 18.8), about 1.45 times a three's per head: 28.6 / 26.1 / 19.7 encounters a head an hour at the start, middle and end, against a three's 19.2 / 18.2 / 15.4. (The Crew scale knob on this page isn't read since the one pacing model went in, so it can't fix this; two new settings can.) Your choices: (1) A crew of two at 0.6 of today's load (crewLoad 2: 0.6). With (2) it gives 21.5 / 18.3 / 13.1 a head an hour, 13.5 monsters a night instead of 19.5; crews of three and more untouched. Or 0.67 (a gentler cut), or as is. (2) Frontier's end eased: the night rises to x3 at the terminus instead of x4 (escalationTier frontier: 2); the start is the same and it still rises. For a crew of three the end goes from 15.4 to 12.2 a head an hour. Or 1.5 (x2.5; a crew of two's end halved), or as is. (3) Repeats: the variety settings barely change anything, because on a moving train the Cinder Hounds are often the only creature that fits. With (1), back-to-back repeats for two fell from 16% to 3%. A real fix is code: hold instead of sending the same creature again when it's the only fit, and let more creatures onto a moving train. Say if you want it. (4) A breather after a fight: (1) alone makes the gaps of 90 s or more go from 21% to 34%. A pause after every fight won, longer for a small crew, is code: say if you want it. Nothing has changed in the game until you answer.

measured.unit: encounters a head an hour: gate, middle, end; frontier:7, seeds 1-6, dt harness --as-app
